sentences.text: Xinjiangovenator is a genus of coelurosaurian dinosaurs that may belong to the group Maniraptora.

The genus is based on a single holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — consisting of an articulated partial right lower leg including the tibia, fibula fragments, ankle bones, and fused foot bones.
This lower leg, comprising the tibia and ankle bones, measures 31.2 cm in length.
Researchers identified a unique trait where the lateral ankle joint at the bottom of the tibia extends further back than the outer edge of the tibia near the knee.
A second unique trait is a longitudinal groove along the front edge of the upper part of the fibula near the knee.
Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that individuals of this genus reached a length of 3 meters and a mass of 70 kilograms.
The remains of Xinjiangovenator were first described by Dong Zhiming in 1973 from fossils found in the Lianmuqin Formation of Wuerho, Xinjiang, China.
Oliver Rauhut and Xu Xing established the new genus Xinjiangovenator in 2005 after realizing the holotype hindlimb bones could not be assigned to the tooth-based genus Phaedrolosaurus.
Rauhut and Xu originally placed Xinjiangovenator within the Maniraptora subgroup of coelurosaurs based on a phylogenetic analysis in 2005.
The analysis suggested Xinjiangovenator was more closely related to paravians like dromaeosaurids and birds than to oviraptorosaurians and therizinosaurs.
Some phylogenetic trees suggest Xinjiangovenator is the sister taxon to Ornitholestes, based on the upper tibia being equally wide at the front and rear edges.
Xinjiangovenator lived between 137.05 and 100.5 million years ago, spanning the Valanginian to Albian stages.
It is debated whether Xinjiangovenator is a basal maniraptoran, as removing it from analysis revealed Ornitholestes to be the basal form instead.
